Anthropic just cut agentic AI task costs by up to 45 percent with its new Claude Fable 5.1 release.

As developers, we are constantly balancing model performance against API costs. The latest updates from Anthropic and Google show that the industry is actively responding to these pricing and capability bottlenecks.

Here is what you need to know from today's releases:

🚀 Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 on Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry, while restricting Claude Mythos 5.1 to vetted organizations under Project Glasswing.

📈 Claude Fable 5.1 features a 1M token context window and scored 52.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, more than doubling the 24.7% score of Fable 5.

💸 Fable 5.1 is up to 45% cheaper for complex agentic tasks, with cache reads reduced by 75% down to $0.25 per million tokens while base pricing holds at $10 and $50.

🎥 Google introduced agentic video understanding with Gemini, expanding how the model processes video inputs.

🎓 Google also highlighted Gemini 3.7 Flash in its latest updates, alongside a new promotion offering a 1-year student plan at no cost.

These updates indicate that the next phase of LLM development is less about raw parameter size and more about cost optimization and specialized agentic workflows.

Are you seeing enough cost reduction in your current API pipelines to justify deploying autonomous agents at scale?
